title: ¿Dónde lo has puesto?
blurbEn: Packing for the trip, and the little words that save you repeating the noun: lo, la, los, las.
body:
—¿Has visto mi pasaporte?

—Lo tienes en la mano.

—Ah. ¿Y las maletas?

—Las bajé al coche hace media hora.

—¿Y los billetes?

—Los tengo yo. También tengo tu tarjeta, porque siempre la olvidas.

Mi hermana es muy organizada. Yo no.

Ella prepara las maletas una semana antes; yo las preparo la noche anterior. Ella hace listas y las revisa dos veces. Yo escribo una lista y después no la encuentro.

Por eso viajamos bien juntas. Ella lo controla todo y yo lo disfruto todo.
translationEn:
"Have you seen my passport?"

"You're holding it."

"Ah. And the suitcases?"

"I took them down to the car half an hour ago."

"And the tickets?"

"I've got them. I've also got your card, because you always forget it."

My sister is very organised. I am not.

She packs the suitcases a week ahead; I pack mine the night before. She makes lists and checks them twice. I write a list and then can't find it.

That's why we travel well together. She controls everything and I enjoy everything.

Las.note: Replaces 'las maletas'. The pronoun matches the gender and number of what it stands for.

Los.note: Replaces 'los billetes'. Not the article 'the' here.

phrases.note: The pronoun goes before the verb, never after it — unlike English.
